rules.name: Read-back is not a crossing
rules.statement: Data the product writes only to read back crosses no interface, unless the map records an outside reader.
rules.risk: The map draws the product's own database as an outside edge, so where the product ends disappears.

sites.why: Keeps the product's own database, cache and queue off the outside edge.
Lets a reader the map records overturn that exclusion, so a store a person browses counts again.
Repeats the same exclusion on the page that fixes every field a map may hold.

rules.name: Name the far side, never the pipe
rules.statement: A step names the service on the far side, never the proxy or the library that carries the call.
rules.risk: The map names the log shipper and never the log store, so the reader cannot tell who receives the data.

sites.why: Names a reverse proxy and a log shipper as carriers, and the log store as the real edge.
Flags a story step that stops at a carrier standing in front of an interface.
Flags the same shortcut inside shared steps, where one carrier is drawn in every story running them.

rules.name: Every outside system is decided
rules.statement: Each outside system names the interfaces it stands on, or records why it is none, never both.
rules.risk: A deliberate exclusion looks exactly like nobody having looked, so the whole edge of the product stops being trustworthy.

sites.why: Stops a map where an outside system neither claims an interface nor gives a reason.
Stops a system that claims an interface and also gives a reason for having none.
Demands the reason on every outside system that names no interface.

rules.name: Kind says what an interface is
rules.statement: An interface is labelled by what it is, never by what it is for.
rules.risk: A payment service and a crash reporter get labels nobody can compare, so the picture stops grouping the edge.

sites.why: Flags a label that answers what the interface is for, such as payments or analytics.
Catches the same purpose label while one part of the map is still being written.
States that a payment service and a crash reporter are the same kind of thing.

rules.name: Far side comes from the stories
rules.statement: Who stands on the far side of an interface is read from the flows, never written by hand.
rules.risk: A hand-written far side disagrees with the stories, and the reader gets two answers with no way to choose.

sites.why: Takes each person standing at a step next to an interface as its far side.
States that the far side has no field of its own.
Forbids writing the far side by hand, and names the two ways it is worked out.

rules.name: Every crossing takes a door
rules.statement: A person meets the product through an interface at every step, not only the first and the last.
rules.risk: The picture shows one person on both sides of one wall, so the edge of the product reads as optional.

sites.why: Calls a step a crossing when a person is at one end, code at the other, and no interface between.
Reports every such step of a story, so a crossing in the middle is heard about too.
States that a crossing in the middle of a story owes a door like the two ends.

rules.name: Own scheduled work is not an outsider
rules.statement: Work the product schedules for itself is never an outsider, so it crosses no interface.
rules.risk: The map counts its own timer as a customer, so an interface handing data to nobody looks answered.

sites.why: Drops a role that is both a machine and internal from the list of outsiders.
States that the product's own scheduled work is not an actor for the door rule.
